ping.title: Ping
ping.description: Connections are automatically closed after 60 seconds of inactivity. Send a ping message periodically to keep the connection alive.

Request.title: Ping
Request.summary: Client sends ping to test connection and keep alive

Response.title: Pong

ts.description: Request timestamp. Unix milliseconds for most operations; Unix seconds for withdrawals (must match the on-chain EIP-712 struct verified against block.timestamp).

placeOrders.title: Create Orders
placeOrders.description:
Create new orders.
Requires proxy signature, see [proxy signing](/http/signing#2-proxy-signing).

<Badge color="gray" size="md">Action Weight: **1 / order**</Badge>

Request.name: PlaceOrdersRequest
Request.title: Create Orders Request
Request.summary: Client submits a signed order placement request

tr.description: Optional trigger attached to this order.

market.description: Whether the trigger executes as a market order

ts.description: Request timestamp. Unix milliseconds for most operations; Unix seconds for withdrawals (must match the on-chain EIP-712 struct verified against block.timestamp).

exp.description: Command expiry timestamp in Unix milliseconds. If provided, it must be in the future and within the gateway's default command timeout. It can shorten request validity but cannot extend it. This is not an order auto-cancel time.

Response.name: PlaceOrdersResponse
Response.title: Create Orders Response
Response.summary: Server responds with order ACK for each submitted order

error.description: Error identifier. For domain rejections and transport errors (`401`/`404`/`429`/`500`) this is a stable, machine-readable snake_case identifier that is part of the API contract and safe to branch on, e.g. `insufficient_margin`, `insufficient_balance`, `order_not_found`, `reduce_only_invalid`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`. For `400` it is a human-readable validation detail whose wording may change. See the Error handling guide for the domain identifiers. (Post-only / Fill-or-Kill outcomes are order statuses such as `post_only_rejected`, not rejections.)

For domain rejections and transport errors (`401`/`404`/`429`/`500`) this is a stable, machine-readable snake_case identifier that is part of the API contract and safe to branch on, e.g. `insufficient_margin`, `insufficient_balance`, `order_not_found`, `reduce_only_invalid`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`. For `400` it is a human-readable validation detail whose wording may change. See the Error handling guide for the domain identifiers. (Post-only / Fill-or-Kill outcomes are order statuses such as `post_only_rejected`, not rejections.)

ts.description: Request timestamp. Unix milliseconds for most operations; Unix seconds for withdrawals (must match the on-chain EIP-712 struct verified against block.timestamp).

size.description: Signed position size in no. of contracts (positive = long, negative = short)

cross.description: Whether to use cross margin mode

return_on_equity.description: Return on equity as a decimal

total_account_value.description: Total account value in USD (equity + unrealized PnL)

total_initial_margin.description: Total initial margin in use across all positions

total_maintenance_margin.description: Total maintenance margin across all positions

total_position_value.description: Total notional position value in USD

in_liquidation.description: Whether the account is currently under liquidation
